Dana — following up with the detailed answers below and attached evidence. Please find an executive summary attached (redwood_dpia_summary.pdf) and our SOC 2 snapshot.

Short answers (high level):
- Do we use customer data to train shared models? No, Redwood’s hosted inference (default) does not incorporate customer prompts/responses into public shared model training. We maintain operational logs for debugging and service quality; those logs are subject to retention controls described below.
- Opt-out mechanisms: Customers can request (a) data exclusion from operational logs used for aggregate telemetry, and (b) a dedicated private deployment (Dedicated/Private) where customer data never leaves their VPC; both options are provided contractually. We also support an opt-out flag at the tenant level for hosted customers; once enabled, telemetry and prompt retention for that tenant are disabled for learning/analytics pipelines.
- Retention timelines: Default raw prompt/response retention for hosted accounts is 30 days for debugging/trace; aggregated telemetry and metrics are retained longer (90–365 days depending on metric type). Customer-requested retention changes are supported via contract (DPA addendum) and technical configuration.
- Contractual & technical controls: We provide a standard DPA, SCCs (for EU transfers), and enterprise Private deployments for regulated workloads. For HIPAA, we offer Business Associate Agreement (BAA) addenda for eligible customers and recommend Private deployment with customer-managed key options.

Attachments in this email: redwood_dpia_summary.pdf (executive DPIA summary), soc2-snapshot-2026-06.pdf (control matrix excerpt), data-retention-policy-v2.docx (policy excerpt).

Technical notes (for Marcus / FinHealth tech reviewers):
- Model training: Redwood’s model catalog contains curated open models and vendor models; Redwood does not perform continual cross-customer fine-tuning on hosted request data. Any model updates are managed by our Research/APL team and occur from internally curated datasets or customer-approved fine-tuning jobs when under a separate contract.
- Telemetry isolation: Operational logs are tenant-tagged. The opt-out flag prevents telemetry from flowing into analytics pipelines and long-term stores used for ML feature extraction (we retain short-term traces for incident diagnostics unless explicitly purged).

Let me know if you want a short 30-minute call to walk through the technical controls and evidence.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Dana / team — I’m Neha (Privacy Counsel) — thanks for the questions. A couple of clarifications from a contractual/compliance perspective:

1) DPA/SCCs: We can execute Redwood’s standard DPA including SCCs (2021/2024 clauses as required). For transfers to US-based processing, SCCs are included and we offer technical safeguards (encryption at rest, customer-managed key on Private).
2) HIPAA: We can sign a BAA for PHI processed in our Dedicated or Private deployments. Hosted accounts may require Private deployment or a specific contractual scope for HIPAA workloads.
3) Opt-out timing: Tenant-level opt-out is typically effective within 48 hours of request; for retroactive purging we coordinate a scoped purge and provide verification logs. Purge verification and audit evidence can be provided as an addendum to the DPA.

We’ve attached the DPIA summary and can provide a fuller DPIA if needed. If you have specific data categories (PHI fields, EU special categories), send them and we’ll map controls.

Regards,
